items.t: Said House Democrats should have a third party handle internal complaints rather than self-policing.
items.q: House Minority Leader Tony McCombie at a Republican Day event at the State Fair on Thursday was critical of the working group and said the House Dems should have a third party handling internal complaints, rather than self-policing.

items.t: Said a work group is not needed to take up the ethics bills that are already out there.
items.q: Even the governor has concerns with this work group. You don't need to have a work group to take some of our ethics bills that are already out there,” McCombie said.

items.t: Was critical of the Speaker's unwritten rule requiring at least 60 House Democrats to support a bill before it is called.
items.q: McCombie was also critical of Welch for his “unwritten rule of 60,” where he requires a minimum of 60 House Dems to support a piece of legislation before it is called in the chamber

items.t: Named fiscal stability, education, growth, and public safety as her main priorities.
items.q: Her main priorities remain in fiscal stability, education, growth, and public safety.

record.t: Joined Illinois State Police officials and the Talbot family at the dedication of the Master Sergeant Stanley Talbot Memorial Bridge in Rock Island.
record.q: officials from Illinois State Police (ISP) and the Talbot family were joined by State Senator Neil Anderson, State Representative Tony McCombie
Tony was elected in 2016 and actively travels the district and pushes to end the culture of corruption and complacency in Springfield.

record.t: Served as Mayor of Savanna, Illinois, before becoming a state representative.
record.q: As State Representative and previous Mayor of Savanna, Illinois, Tony McCombie has a proven, nonpartisan record of finding ways to work together
